scope: Current-source screening for SFF partner rows that have both an explicit San Francisco service or audience signal and a verified current charitable receiving route.
method: A screening record can preserve identity, reach, evidence, financial transparency, and next-dollar gaps. It cannot promote a partner into the six-organization comparison or recommendation slate without a program-specific marginal plan, a durable outcome, a defensible counterfactual, and an inspectable conversion model where used.

entity.donationBoundary: El Tímpano's current page says donations route through Mission Edge and are tax deductible to the full extent of the law. Market for Impact does not provide tax advice.

serviceGeography.label: Bay Area Latino and Mayan immigrant communities
serviceGeography.sanFranciscoSignal: More than 100 SMS subscribers in San Francisco at the start of 2025.
serviceGeography.boundary: Subscriber presence is not a San Francisco-specific program, outcome cohort, expenditure allocation, or marginal funding plan.

intervention.type: community-centered journalism, two-way SMS news and resource navigation, participatory reporting, and civic partnerships
intervention.theoryOfChange: Trusted, language-accessible information and two-way reporting may improve access to relevant news and services, strengthen civic self-efficacy, and help institutions respond to community needs.
intervention.causalBoundary: Subscribers, messages, replies, questions, events, and partnerships are reach or engagement signals. They do not establish service uptake, changed behavior, durable wellbeing, policy change, QALYs, WELLBYs, or lives substantially bettered.

nativeSignals.label: SMS subscriber community
nativeSignals.limitation: The first annual survey received 175 responses; subscriber count is not an outcome and survey respondents may not represent all subscribers.

nativeSignals.label: First-half SMS engagement
nativeSignals.limitation: The report does not deduplicate people across replies and questions or connect engagement to service uptake or durable outcomes.

nativeSignals.label: Inaugural resource fair
nativeSignals.limitation: Attendance and partner presence do not identify resources received, successful referrals, incremental access, or follow-up outcomes.

nativeSignals.label: Civic-partnership revenue
nativeSignals.limitation: This is one revenue stream described in a 2026 playbook announcement, not total project revenue, unrestricted cash, expenses, or philanthropic room for more funding.

financials.boundary: Mission Edge's organization-wide filings would cover many sponsored projects and cannot be assigned to El Tímpano. Public donor tiers and one partnership-revenue figure do not reconcile total revenue, expenses, restrictions, cash, liabilities, runway, or a current funding gap.

evidenceLayers.title: 2024 Midyear Impact Report
evidenceLayers.finding: The report describes regional newsroom growth, 83 SMS bulletins, 2,455 direct responses, 188 answered questions, and a resource fair with more than 600 attendees and 30 partner organizations.
evidenceLayers.decisionUse: Establishes a bounded operating and engagement baseline for a future marginal plan.
evidenceLayers.transferLimit: The source is organization-authored and does not provide a comparison group, deduplicated participant denominator, service-uptake verification, durable outcomes, project-level finances, or San Francisco-only results.

evidenceLayers.title: Who makes up El Tímpano's SMS community
evidenceLayers.design: descriptive subscriber records and first annual survey; 175 respondents
evidenceLayers.finding: The source profiles a community of more than 5,500 subscribers, reports geographic distribution including more than 100 San Francisco subscribers, and describes respondents' occupations, education, technology access, and information sources.
evidenceLayers.decisionUse: Defines who the SMS channel reaches and makes the small explicit San Francisco audience signal auditable.
evidenceLayers.transferLimit: The survey is descriptive, voluntary, and small relative to the subscriber base. It does not estimate causal changes in knowledge, service use, behavior, civic participation, or wellbeing.

evidenceLayers.title: Community-Centered Outlets Empower and Inform Latinos
evidenceLayers.design: preregistered randomized controlled trial with more than 350 participants across El Tímpano and two peer outlets; eight-week exposure
evidenceLayers.finding: The research summary reports higher political self-efficacy and stated voting intention among participants exposed to community-centered outlet content than among participants assigned to traditional outlets.
evidenceLayers.decisionUse: Supports a plausible near-term civic-information pathway and identifies self-efficacy, knowledge, and stated participation as measurable intermediate outcomes.
evidenceLayers.transferLimit: The public summary pools three outlets and does not isolate El Tímpano, San Francisco subscribers, actual turnout, service access, policy change, durable wellbeing, or cost-effectiveness. Stated intention is not observed behavior.

evidenceLayers.title: El Tímpano releases Civic Partnerships Playbook to help local newsrooms build sustainable revenue
evidenceLayers.finding: The announcement reports $350,000 in 2025 contracts with government and nonprofit agencies and says the outlet reached more than 6,600 SMS subscribers by May 2026.
evidenceLayers.decisionUse: Identifies one material revenue stream, a newer reach baseline, and potential funder-displacement questions for a future marginal plan.
evidenceLayers.transferLimit: The announcement is not an audited or complete project financial statement. Partnership revenue is not total revenue, unrestricted cash, profit, philanthropic funding room, an impact estimate, or a San Francisco allocation.

evidenceLayers.title: From Soil to City Hall: How El Tímpano Reporters Put Oakland's Lead Problem on the Agenda
evidenceLayers.design: funder-published reporting and engagement case study
evidenceLayers.finding: The case study documents a reporting-and-engagement sequence around lead exposure that included a Spanish-language workshop, community partners, public officials, and a panel discussion.
evidenceLayers.decisionUse: Shows the observable steps in one information-to-engagement pathway and suggests concrete milestones for a future funded project.
evidenceLayers.transferLimit: A project case study is not a counterfactual evaluation. It does not estimate El Tímpano's causal effect on lead remediation, exposure, health, policy, or resident wellbeing and concerns Oakland rather than San Francisco.

fundingRoom.boundary: The public donation page and supporter list do not identify a time-bounded marginal project, capacity, expected co-funding, displacement, milestones, or incremental outcomes at any requested gift size.

reviews.decisionSummary: El Tímpano has a verified charitable receiving route, an explicit but small San Francisco audience signal, unusually rich two-way engagement data, and pooled randomized evidence for its intervention class. It remains outside the comparison and recommendation slate because accepted sources do not publish an El Tímpano-specific causal effect, a durable San Francisco outcome, reconciled project finances, or a marginal funding plan.
missingForRecommendation: A San Francisco-specific cohort and common denominator for reach, replies, answered questions, successful referrals, verified service uptake, knowledge, behavior, and durable outcomes.
El Tímpano-specific causal measurement that separates the SMS channel, reporting, resource navigation, events, and partner activity from the pooled three-outlet trial.
Project-level revenue, expenses, restrictions, cash, liabilities, runway, staff and platform capacity, and reconciliation with Mission Edge and disclosed donors or public-agency partners.

A time-bounded marginal plan at $100,000, $1 million, and $10 million that names the additional program, audience, activities, co-funding, displacement risk, milestones, and stop rules—or says an amount cannot be productively absorbed.

A versioned path from information access and engagement to a durable MFI outcome, with adverse effects, privacy and source-safety risks, uncertainty, and any QALY, WELLBY, or life-substantially-bettered translation kept blocked until defensible.
